# core


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

Vāgdhenu ([code](https://github.com/prathoshap/vagdhenu),
[weights](https://huggingface.co/prathoshap/vagdhenu), Apache-2.0) is an
IndicF5 fine-tune with a BigVGAN-v2 vocoder, trained on one speaker’s
chant. Its source, BigVGAN’s and IndicF5’s (`f5_tts`, which differs from
the `f5-tts` on PyPI) are not pip packages, so all three are fetched at
pinned commits into the cache on first use and put on `sys.path`. The
weights come from the Hub.

## Text

The model reads plain Devanagari. Vedic accents, digits, and verse
numbers between daṇḍas are dropped. Vāgdhenu has no svaras and is for
laukika chant.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/vachaka/blob/main/vachaka/core.py#L53"

### chunk_prose

``` python
def chunk_prose(
    text, max_syll:int=24
):
```

*Split prose at daṇḍas, then at word breaks, into pieces of at most
`max_syll` akṣaras.*

``` python
p = chunk_prose('अथातो धर्मजिज्ञासा । चोदनालक्षणोऽर्थो धर्मः । तस्य निमित्तपरीष्टिः ॥')
test_eq(p, ['अथातो धर्मजिज्ञासा', 'चोदनालक्षणोऽर्थो धर्मः', 'तस्य निमित्तपरीष्टिः'])
assert all(n_syll(c) <= 24 for c in chunk_prose('क '*80))
```

## Sound

Named treatments for someone who is not a sound engineer, chosen by ear.
Each ends in loudness normalisation (-16 LUFS), so every title plays at
the same volume, and none moves a sound in time: an echo adds decay
after a syllable, never delay before it, so the line and word timings
hold. `warm` is the default: a little warmth below 250 Hz, a soft
de-esser and the short echo of a small room. `phone` lifts the words for
small speakers.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a

## Recitation

The rendered audio with one `(start_ms, end_ms)` span per piece. Each
piece is a line given to
[`Chanter.chant`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vachaka/core.html#chanter.chant),
or a chunk from
[`Chanter.read`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vachaka/core.html#chanter.read).

## Chanter

Loads the DiT, the vocoder and the reference bank once. `pace` stretches
every syllable (1.15 by default: unhurried, for chanting along). On
Apple silicon the DiT runs on MPS and BigVGAN on the CPU, since MPS
lacks a transposed convolution with more than 65,536 output channels.
`chant` renders verse against the bank’s reference for the metre
[ganapati](https://github.com/vedicreader/ganapati) scans it as; `read`
renders prose against the gadya reference by default. The reference sets
pace and melody; the timbre is the fine-tuned voice.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/vachaka/blob/main/vachaka/core.py#L151"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Chanter

``` python
def Chanter(
    voice:str='steer', device:NoneType=None, nfe:int=64, speed:float=0.9, gap:float=0.55, prose_gap:float=0.3,
    tail:float=0.18, fade:float=0.12, pad:float=0.5, pace:float=1.15
):
```

*Sanskrit verse and prose to audio with line spans.*

Rendering needs the weights (about 1.5 GB on first use) and takes
several times real time on Apple silicon, so these cells do not run in
the tests.

``` python
ch = Chanter()
r = ch.chant(['वसुदेवसुतं देवं कंसचाणूरमर्दनम्', 'देवकीपरमानन्दं कृष्णं वन्दे जगद्गुरुम्'])
r.spans, r.save('/tmp/krishna.mp3')
```

``` python
ch.read('अथातो धर्मजिज्ञासा । चोदनालक्षणोऽर्थो धर्मः ।').save('/tmp/mimamsa.mp3')
```
